data.body_html:
Cabopino’s coastline is a hidden gem for sunset photography, with its dunes, pine forests, and iconic lighthouse. A Cabopino boat rental for sunset photography gives you unrivalled angles from the water. Our fleet departs Puerto Banús, just 15 minutes east, and includes boats from €749/2h. Whether you’re capturing the golden light on La Concha or the silhouette of the Cabopino lighthouse, here’s how to make the most of your charter.

Why Choose a Boat for Cabopino Sunset Photography?

From land, the Cabopino coastline is beautiful. From the water, you get unobstructed 360-degree views. The reflection of the sun on the Mediterranean, the silhouette of the Sierra Blanca, and the distant Gibraltar — all frame your shots. A boat lets you reposition quickly as the light changes. Plus, you avoid the crowds on the beach.

Best Cabopino Spots for Sunset Photos

Cala del Faro — the lighthouse at the eastern end of Cabopino beach. Shoot from the water with the lighthouse in the foreground and the sun setting behind La Concha. Cala Cortés — a rocky cove with dramatic cliffs. The texture of the rocks catches warm light beautifully. Cabopino Dunes — anchor near the sandbar and capture the dunes with the sun sinking into the sea. For a wider scene, head west towards the Golden Mile where the Marbella skyline appears.

Camera Settings & Gear for Boat-Based Sunset Photography

Bring a tripod (carbon fibre is lighter). Use a wide-angle lens (16-35mm) for landscapes and a telephoto (70-200mm) for compression shots of the lighthouse. Settings: aperture f/8-f/11 for sharpness, ISO 100-400, shutter speed 1/30 to 1/125 depending on light. For long exposures of the sea, use an ND filter and shutter speeds of 2-30 seconds. Shoot in RAW for better post-processing. Don’t forget a polariser to cut glare on the water.

Which Boat Is Right for Your Photography Charter?

For solo or duo photographers, the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) is agile and easy to manoeuvre close to shore. Groups of up to 10 will love the Pershing 46 (14m) with its open cockpit. For the ultimate stable platform, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) offers a large flybridge and bow area — perfect for tripods. All boats include a licensed skipper who knows the best anchor spots.

Timing Your Charter for the Perfect Light

In Marbella, sunset times vary: June 21:30, September 20:00, December 18:00. Book a 4-hour charter starting 2 hours before sunset. This gives you golden hour (warm, low-angle light), the sunset itself, and blue hour (twilight) for long exposures. The skipper can adjust the route based on the sun’s position. A 2-hour charter is enough for a quick shoot but may feel rushed.

What’s Included in Your Sunset Charter

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and safety equipment. Spanish IVA (21%) is included. You only need to bring your camera gear, a jacket (it can get breezy at sea), and a sense of adventure. The skipper will help you find the best anchor spots for your photos.

Tips for a Successful Sunset Photography Boat Trip

  • Arrive 15 minutes early to set up gear while the boat is stationary.
  • Use a lens hood to avoid lens flare from the sun.
  • Shoot multiple exposures (bracketing) for HDR later.
  • Include the boat’s bow or a crew member for scale.
  • Check the weather forecast — clear skies are best, but a few clouds add drama.
  • Bring a waterproof bag for your camera.

Frequently asked questions

Can I rent a boat directly from Cabopino Marina?

Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, about 15 minutes east by boat. We don’t have boats moored at Cabopino Marina, but the short cruise along the coast is part of the experience.

What is the best time for sunset photography on a boat?

Golden hour starts about 2 hours before sunset. In Marbella, that’s typically 18:30–20:30 in summer and 17:00–19:00 in winter. Book a 4-hour charter to cover both golden hour and twilight.

Which boat is best for a photography charter?

The Mangusta 80 (24m) offers a spacious flybridge and bow area for tripods. For smaller groups, the Azimut 39 (11 pax) is stable and affordable. All boats have open decks.

Do you provide photography equipment?

No, we only provide the boat, skipper, drinks, and snacks. Bring your own camera, tripod, and any filters. We recommend a wide-angle lens for landscapes and a telephoto for wildlife.

What are the best sunset photo spots near Cabopino?

Cala del Faro (lighthouse), Cala Cortés (rock formations), and the Cabopino dunes with La Concha mountain in the background. Anchoring near the Cabopino sandbar gives you both sea and mountain.

Can I swim during the sunset charter?

Yes, we can anchor at a quiet cove. Most sunset charters include a stop for swimming. Just let the skipper know your preference. Life jackets are onboard.

What is the cancellation policy?

You can cancel up to 48 hours before departure for a full refund. Weather cancellations are free. Rescheduling is always possible subject to availability.

Is the sunset charter suitable for non-photographers?

Absolutely. The sunset cruise is a relaxed experience with drinks and snacks. Non-photographers enjoy the views, swimming, and atmosphere. It’s a social outing for all.
